## IFocusPouch

```java
public interface IFocusPouch
```

An item that stores focuses for the wand's focus selector: the native focus pouch, and a pouch of an add-on.

TC4 did not have this interface. Its selector (the change focus key) found a pouch by the class `ItemFocusPouch` and read the foci in it with `getInventory(ItemStack)`; Thaumic Tinkerer's Bottomless Pouch extended that class with 117 cells. `getInventory` and `setInventory(ItemStack, ItemStack[])` keep the original names and become this interface, so an add-on pouch is offered by the selector exactly like the native one without extending an internal class.

What the selector does with a pouch (an item of the stack implements this interface):
- It looks at the 36 main inventory slots (hotbar included) and at the four accessory slots, so a pouch that is also a belt `thaumcraft.api.baubles.IBauble` is listed while worn. The off-hand, the armour slots and the contents of other containers are not looked at. Only a stack of exactly one pouch counts.
- It lists every cell that holds a focus (an `ItemFocusBasic` that can be mounted). Other items in a cell are ignored and never touched. The selector UI is a ring with one button per focus, not a grid, so a pouch of any size is listed; only the first `MAX_SELECTABLE_CELLS` cells are listed (the native pouch has 18).
- When the player picks a focus, it leaves its cell (the cell becomes `ItemStack.EMPTY`) and is mounted on the wand; the focus the wand had goes into the first empty cell among the first `MAX_SELECTABLE_CELLS` cells of the first pouch that has one (worn pouches first, then the main inventory, each from its first cell), before any free inventory slot. The selection is all or nothing.
- A right click never puts a pouch into an accessory slot, whatever `thaumcraft.api.baubles.IBauble.equipsOnUse` answers: the click goes to the pouch's own `use`, which normally opens its screen. It is put on in the Baubles menu.

The pouch does its own storage, typically in a data component, and its own screen. Opening a screen, the rules for what may be put in, the number of cells and their layout are all the add-on's.

<a id="ifocuspouch-max_selectable_cells"></a>
```java
int MAX_SELECTABLE_CELLS
```

The most cells of one pouch the focus selector reads and writes: the cells whose index is this number or more are neither listed nor given a returned focus. Thaumic Tinkerer's pouch has 117 cells, which fit.

<a id="ifocuspouch-getinventory"></a>
```java
ItemStack[] getInventory(ItemStack pouch)
```

All cells of the pouch, in order, with `ItemStack.EMPTY` for an empty cell (never `null`).

The length is the pouch's number of cells and must be the same on every call for the same pouch stack. Every stack of the result is an independent copy: the caller changes the array and its stacks freely, and a change reaches the pouch only through `setInventory`. Called on both logical sides: on the client to list the focuses, on the server to select one.

A stack that carries a payload this pouch cannot read (for example saved by another version) throws `IllegalArgumentException`; the selector then ignores that pouch and leaves its payload untouched. Any other `RuntimeException` is treated the same way (and written to the log once per pouch class), because the selector also asks on the client's render thread, where an add-on's bug would otherwise close the game; do not rely on that, an exception is the way to say "unreadable", not to report an error.

**Returns:** the cells, a new array

**Throws:** `IllegalArgumentException` — if the stack holds contents this pouch cannot read

**Parameters:**
- `pouch` — one pouch of this item; its stack count is one

<a id="ifocuspouch-setinventory"></a>
```java
void setInventory(ItemStack pouch, ItemStack[] contents)
```

Replaces all cells of the pouch.

`contents` has the length `getInventory` returned for this stack; an entry is `ItemStack.EMPTY` for an empty cell. Copy what is kept: the caller may still hold the array. Change nothing but the given stack. Called on the server thread only; the selector calls it on the live stack of the player's inventory or accessory slot (the same stack object stays in its slot) and also on a scratch copy of a stack while it plans a selection, so it must not have any effect outside the stack it is given. It may not refuse an array `getInventory` could have returned with one cell changed.

If it throws anyway (a `RuntimeException`, written to the log once per pouch class), the selection stays all or nothing: while the selector plans on a scratch copy, the pouch gives no focus and takes none; if it throws on the live stack, the selection is refused and every stack it had already written is put back as it was, so the wand keeps its focus and no focus is lost or duplicated. A pouch that wrote part of its payload before throwing is therefore restored by the selector, not by the pouch.

**Throws:** `IllegalArgumentException` — if `contents` has the wrong length

**Parameters:**
- `pouch` — one pouch of this item; its stack count is one
- `contents` — the new cells, one entry per cell, none `null`

## IWandRodOnUpdate

```java
public interface IWandRodOnUpdate
```

The original TC4 wand rod update hook.

Add-on contract (original ItemWandCasting.onUpdate:350-355): the hook of an add-on `WandRod` is called on the **server** once per tick for every wand, staff or sceptre with that rod in a player's inventory, with the live stack and its carrier. It may change the stack's vis through `ItemWandCasting.addVis/addRealVis` (whole vis / centivis); the stack is the inventory's own, so a change is saved and synchronised like any inventory change. Native rods refill through the port's own passive and never call their views' hooks.

Forced 1.21.1 change: `EntityPlayer` became `Player`.

```java
void onUpdate(ItemStack stack, Player player)
```

## IWandable

```java
public interface IWandable
```

The original TC4 wand contract: a block, or a block entity, that answers a click with a wand, staff or sceptre.

Original ItemWandCasting: the block is asked first, then its block entity, before the registered wand triggers and the native wand interactions.

Forced 1.21.1 changes: `EntityPlayer` became `Player` and `World` became `Level`.

<a id="iwandable-onwandrightclick"></a>
```java
int onWandRightClick(Level level, ItemStack stack, Player player, int x, int y, int z, int side, int event)
```

The original click on the block (ItemWandCasting.onItemUseFirst), on both sides.

**Returns:** a negative value when the click was not handled (the wand goes on with its own behaviour); otherwise the click is handled and nothing else happens: 1 swings the arm (success), any other value is a quiet failure

**Parameters:**
- `side` — the clicked face, as `Direction.get3DDataValue()`
- `event` — the block metadata in 1.7.10; always 0 in 1.21.1

<a id="iwandable-onwandrightclick-2"></a>
```java
ItemStack onWandRightClick(Level level, ItemStack stack, Player player)
```

The original click without a target (ItemWandCasting.onItemRightClick), asked of the block the player looks at.

**Returns:** the stack the hand holds afterwards when the click was handled, or `null` when it was not


## StaffRod

```java
public class StaffRod extends WandRod
```

The original TC4 staff rod: a rod with the staff tag and its own texture.

Add-on contract: everything of `WandRod` applies; the rod is registered under `<tag>_staff`, and a wand built from it is a staff (original `isStaff`: `rod instanceof StaffRod`) - the long staff model, +6 attack damage, no arcane workbench slot. `setRunes(boolean)` adds the primal staff's runes and one focus potency. The capacity is in whole vis (the original staves declare 125 / 175 / 250). The derived texture is the sheet of the plain rod, `thaumcraft:textures/models/wand_rod_<tag>.png`, and the wand name uses `item.Wand.<tag>.rod`.

Forced 1.21.1 change: the original staff texture name is kept, but the native staff rods are the `<rod>_staff` entries of the native rod catalogue, present in `WandRod.rods` as `StaffRod` views.

## WandCap

```java
public class WandCap
```

The original TC4 wand cap.

 <h2>Add-on contract</h2>

An add-on registers a cap exactly like it did on 1.7.10, by constructing it; the constructor puts it into `caps` under its tag:

```java
WandCap alchemical = new WandCap("alchemical", 0.9F, List.of(Aspect.WATER), 0.8F, new ItemStack(MyItems.ALCHEMICAL_CAP), 7);
alchemical.setTexture(ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath("myaddon", "textures/models/wand_cap_alchemical.png"));
```
- **Discount** is the vis cost multiplier of the wand (1 is unchanged, 0.9 is a tenth cheaper); an aspect of the special list uses the special multiplier instead (original ItemWandCasting.getConsumptionModifier:243-248). The equipment discount, the frugal upgrade and the sceptre are subtracted from it as usual, never below a tenth.
- **Craft cost** is the dimensionless assembly factor, multiplied with the rod's (see `WandRod`).
- **Item** is the stack the arcane workbench accepts in the two (sceptre: three) cap cells, compared like the original.
- **Research** is `getResearch()`, `CAP_<tag>`; the add-on registers it itself.
- **Texture** is an entity-style sheet in the layout of the original `ModelWand` cap (the 1.7.10 PNG works unchanged); the constructors derive `thaumcraft:textures/models/wand_cap_<tag>.png`, so an add-on calls `setTexture`.
- **Name**: the wand name uses the translation key `item.Wand.<tag>.cap`; the add-on ships it in its own lang file.

Registration may happen at any time of mod initialisation; gameplay looks the registry up whenever it needs a cap, so later setter calls are seen. The registry is a plain map: register during initialisation only.

 <h2>Native caps</h2>

The native caps of the port's catalogue are present in `caps` as views (`nativeCap()` is non-null) with the original values. Gameplay reads native caps from the catalogue: changing a native view, or registering another cap under a native tag, does not change the native cap (forced deviation that keeps the native values bit-identical).

<a id="wandcap-caps"></a>
```java
public static LinkedHashMap<String, WandCap> caps
```

The original public registry; it stays mutable so an add-on may add its own cap. Native views are registered first.


Registers (or replaces) a cap without special aspects; retains a nullable item.

**Parameters:**

- `craftCost` — the dimensionless assembly factor


Registers (or replaces) a cap whose special aspects use their own multiplier; retains the nullable item/aspect list.

**Parameters:**
- `discount` — the vis cost multiplier of every other aspect (1 means unchanged)
- `specialAspects` — the aspects that use `discountSpecial`; may be null
- `discountSpecial` — the vis cost multiplier of the special aspects

## WandHelper

```java
public final class WandHelper
```

The public methods of the original `thaumcraft.common.items.wands.ItemWandCasting` that add-ons called, as static methods of the API, so a ported add-on never needs the internal wand item.

A 1.7.10 call `((ItemWandCasting) stack.getItem()).addVis(stack, Aspect.FIRE, 1, true)` becomes `WandHelper.addVis(stack, Aspect.FIRE, 1, true)`. Every method accepts any stack: a stack that is not a wand, staff or sceptre (`isWand`) answers "nothing" (null, zero, an empty list, false) and is never changed.

 <h2>Units</h2>
- The wand stores **centivis** (hundredths of vis), like the original NBT: `getVis`, `getAllVis`, `getMaxVis`, `addRealVis`, `consumeVis` and `consumeAllVis` speak centivis (`ItemFocusBasic.getVisCost` is centivis too).
- `addVis` and `consumeAllVisCrafting` speak **whole vis** and multiply by a hundred, like the original.
- `WandRod.getCapacity()` is whole vis; `getMaxVis` is its centivis capacity (times 1.5 for a sceptre).

<h2>Authority</h2>

The wand's vis is server state that the inventory synchronises. Change it on the logical server. The methods that take a player answer exactly as the original but leave the stack unchanged when that player is on the client (the original `consumeAllVis` already did so; `consumeVis` did not), so a focus may call them on both sides and the client waits for the server's copy. The methods without a player change the stack they are given.

## WandRod

```java
public class WandRod
```

The original TC4 wand rod.

 <h2>Add-on contract</h2>

An add-on registers a rod exactly like it did on 1.7.10, by constructing it; the constructor puts it into `rods` under its tag:

```java
WandRod infernal = new WandRod("infernal", 150, new ItemStack(MyItems.INFERNAL_ROD), 12, new MyRodOnUpdate(),
        ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath("myaddon", "textures/models/wand_rod_infernal.png"));
```
- **Capacity** is in **whole vis**, the unit of the original constructors (`new WandRod("silverwood", 100, ...)`). The wand stores centivis: a wand holds `capacity * 100` centivis of every primal, a sceptre `capacity * 150` (original ItemWandCasting.getMaxVis:91). `getCapacity()` answers whole vis for every rod, native ones included (`WandRod.rods.get("greatwood").getCapacity() == 50`).
- **Craft cost** is the dimensionless assembly factor: the arcane workbench asks `rodCost * capCost` vis of each primal for a wand, and `(int) (rodCost * capCost * 1.5F)` for a sceptre (original ArcaneWandRecipe:59, ArcaneSceptreRecipe:64); the paying wand's cap and the player's gear discount that price as usual.
- **Item** is the stack the arcane workbench accepts in the rod cell; it is compared by item and, when the grid stack carries its own components, by those components (original ArcaneWandRecipe.checkItemEquals).
- **Research** is `getResearch()`, `ROD_<tag>`; the add-on registers that research itself. A subclass may override it.
- **`IWandRodOnUpdate`** is called on the server every tick the wand sits in a player's inventory (original ItemWandCasting.onUpdate:350-355). Use `ItemWandCasting.addVis/getVis/getMaxVis` from it.
- **Texture** is an entity-style sheet in the layout of the original `ModelWand` (the 1.7.10 PNG works unchanged); a texture of null falls back to `thaumcraft:textures/models/wand_rod_<tag>.png`. `setGlowing(boolean)` lights the rod like the original ModelWand:87-101.
- **Name**: the wand name uses the translation key `item.Wand.<tag>.rod` (for a `StaffRod`, the tag without `_staff`); the add-on ships it in its own `lang/*.json`.

Registration may happen at any time of mod initialisation, before or after Thaumcraft, on Fabric or NeoForge: gameplay looks the registry up whenever it needs a part, nothing is copied at Thaumcraft's initialisation, and later setter calls on the registered object are seen. Register during initialisation only: the registry is a plain map, not thread-safe, and a wand whose rod is no longer registered can neither be loaded nor used.

 <h2>Native rods</h2>

The native rods of the port's catalogue (`thaumcraft.common.items.wands.WandMaterials`) are present in `rods` as views (`nativeRod()` is non-null; the nine staff cores are `StaffRod`s), as in the original. Their values are those of the original rods. Gameplay reads native rods from the catalogue, not from these views: changing a native view, or registering another rod under a native tag, does not change the native rod (forced deviation that keeps the native values bit-identical).

Forced 1.21.1 change: the original metadata-free rod is unchanged, but the item is a native `ItemStack` and the texture a `ResourceLocation`, as before.


The original public registry; it stays mutable so an add-on may add its own rod. Native views are registered first.

## WandTriggerRegistry

```java
public class WandTriggerRegistry
```

The original TC4 wand trigger registry.

Forced 1.21.1 change: the original keyed a trigger by block and metadata; 1.21.1 has no block metadata, so a trigger is keyed either by a whole block or by one exact block state. The original metadata argument still exists and is ignored: a block that was registered for one metadata is now registered for all of its states. It cannot express selection among 1.21.1 BlockState properties; metadata dispatch substitutes defaultBlockState. Use BlockState registration/query/dispatch for exact states, or explicit whole-Block forms when every state is intended.


Retained metadata form; `meta` is ignored and every state of the block is registered.

**Deprecated:** Use `hasTrigger(Block, String)` for whole-block registrations or `hasTrigger(BlockState, String)` to include exact-state registrations. Metadata is ignored.

Queries whole-block registrations without dispatching a callback. A null block returns false; a null mod id searches all mods. Exact-state entries are not queried.

Original `WandTriggerRegistry:38-45`: the exact registration of the block and the metadata answered for every registration of the whole block. The native registry keys a trigger either by one exact block state or by the whole block, so the state answer has to consult both forms, exactly like `performTrigger` does. Before this fix the public answer and the public dispatch disagreed for a trigger that was registered for a whole block.

<a id="wandtriggerregistry-performtrigger-2"></a>
```java
public static boolean performTrigger(Level level, ItemStack wand, Player player, int x, int y, int z, int side, Block block, int meta)
```

> **Deprecated.**

The original block and metadata form of the dispatch.

Forced 1.21.1 change: 1.21.1 has no block metadata, so the metadata argument is ignored and the exact state of the block is its default state. The wildcard registration of the whole block is still the fallback, exactly as in the original.

**Deprecated:** Use `performTrigger(Level, ItemStack, Player, int, int, int, int, BlockState)` with the actual clicked state. This overload ignores metadata and uses the block's default state.

<a id="wandtriggerregistry-performtrigger-3"></a>
```java

```

> **Deprecated.**

Retained per-mod dispatch; metadata is ignored and a null block returns false.

**Deprecated:** Use `performTrigger(Level, ItemStack, Player, int, int, int, int, BlockState, String)` with the actual clicked state, not a legacy metadata value.

<a id="wandtriggerregistry-performtrigger-4"></a>
```java
public static boolean performTrigger(Level level, ItemStack wand, Player player, int x, int y, int z, int side, BlockState state, String modid)
```

Dispatches matching callbacks until one returns true; returns false for a null state or no success. Exact-state registrations take precedence over whole-block registrations within each mod. A null mod id searches all mods, with unspecified order between mods. Coordinates are block coordinates and `side` is passed through unchanged. Level, wand and player, including null, are passed to the callback; its side effects and exceptions are not suppressed.


The registered mod ids; the original kept them apart per mod.
